explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/654: with no four points concyclic, is there always a point with > (1−o(1))n distinct distances to the others? Disproved by Aletheia [Fe26], who gave n-point sets with at most 3n/4 distances from every point. The statement negates ∀ ε > 0, ∀ᶠ n, ∀ A with |A| = n and NoFourConcyclic, ∃ x with (1−ε)n < distinctDistancesFrom A x. A counterexample for infinitely many n (n = 4m) refutes the eventual statement with ε = 1/8. Faithful.
